strings: Hidden Enemies is a pivotal step in Warchief Thrall's investigation into cultist infiltration within Orgrimmar. Having executed the ringleaders of the Burning Blade beneath the city, the player is sent to embed themselves further as a confidant to Neeru Fireblade.

Following the assassination of Bazzalan and Jergosh the Invoker in Ragefire Chasm, Thrall recognizes an opening. Rather than exposing Neeru Fireblade directly, the Warchief chooses to play the long game. Neeru is distressed by the sudden loss of his underground lieutenants, creating a void of leadership within the local cult. Thrall dispatches you back to the shadowy recesses of the Cleft of Shadow to present yourself as a dependable ally who can fill that vacuum.

When approached in the Cleft of Shadow, Neeru Fireblade is visibly furious over the sudden defeat of his conspirators. Unaware that the very adventurer standing before him carried out the executions on Thrall's orders, Neeru curses the 'do-gooders' who brought ruin to Ragefire Chasm. Caught off guard by the swift strike, Neeru begins to lower his guard around the player, paving the way for Thrall to monitor the Shadow Council's influence directly from within Orgrimmar.
Why doesn't Thrall just execute Neeru Fireblade immediately?

Thrall prefers keeping an exposed enemy where he can watch them. By leaving Neeru in place while thinking his cover is intact, Thrall can monitor the Burning Blade's communications and trace their ties back to the Shadow Council, using the player as an inside operative.

Hidden Enemies is the culmination of Warchief Thrall's operation to infiltrate and assess the Burning Blade coven lurking inside Orgrimmar. By returning to Thrall after securing the trust of Neeru Fireblade, you provide critical intelligence on the cult's widening reach across Kalimdor.

At Warchief Thrall's request, an operative carried a Lieutenant's Insignia taken at Skull Rock to Neeru Fireblade, a warlock dwelling openly in the Cleft of Shadow, and later struck at the Searing Blade's leaders deep within Ragefire Chasm. By playing the role of a willing recruit and bearing the insignias of fallen cultists, the operative earns Fireblade's trust, leading the warlock to inadvertently reveal the broader network backing his operations.

Thinking he has gained a loyal lieutenant, Neeru Fireblade admits that the loss in Ragefire Chasm is a setback for the Searing Blade, but declares that the Shadow Council's greater designs remain intact. He reveals that his masters have active agents operating not only in the Barrens, but deeper in the forests of Ashenvale. Reporting this news to Thrall catches the Warchief off-guard, revealing that the demonic conspiracy extends far beyond the subterranean tunnels of the capital.

Rather than executing Neeru immediately, Thrall chooses a cautious path. Keeping Neeru unaware of his compromise allows the Horde to monitor his communications and track the cult's tentacles across Durotar, the Barrens, and Ashenvale. The Warchief prepares his scouts and spies to investigate these regional branches, recognizing that rooting out demonic corruption requires precision rather than reckless haste.

This errand sends travelers across the sea from the salt pans of Kalimdor to the steaming jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. Out in the blinding expanse of the Shimmering Flats, commerce moves fast, but shipments sometimes lag behind. Kravel Koalbeard eventually receives a delayed crate earmarked for one of his wealthy patrons, Hemet Nesingwary. Deep within the Royal Library of Stormwind Keep, head librarian Donyal Tovald manages a collection of historical texts and regional accounts. By order of the young King Anduin Wrynn, funds have been allocated to transcribe copies of these works for citizens and scholars who bring official library scrips. This service allows adventurers to study the history, factions, and legends of Azeroth firsthand.

While Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and Lady Katrana Prestor oversee defense and court politics in King Varian's absence, young King Anduin has directed royal resources toward education. Recognizing that understanding history is crucial for the kingdom's future, Anduin sponsored the transcribing of ancient manuscripts and historical journals. The Royal Library, nestled in the halls of Stormwind Keep, serves not merely as a royal vault for state secrets, but as a repository where documented lore is preserved and copied for those in royal service.

Transcribing delicate parchment by hand requires significant time, ink, and royal sanction. To manage this distribution, the head librarian Donyal Tovald accepts official library scrips, issued to adventurers and scholars across Alliance territories. In exchange, Tovald provides faithful duplicates of historical tomes, covering everything from the ancient histories of the Eastern Kingdoms to accounts of distant lands, offering context for ongoing conflicts beyond the capital's walls.

Moonglade is an introductory rite of passage for young night elf druids learning to commune with the sacred lands of Kalimdor. Guided by Mathrengyl Bearwalker in Darnassus, novices learn the spell to magically transport themselves across the world into Moonglade to meet Dendrite Starblaze in Nighthaven. This marks the beginning of their spiritual journey toward mastering the strength of the bear form.

Moonglade stands apart from the rest of Azeroth as an ancient sanctuary dedicated to the teachings of Cenarius. Under the watchful stewardship of Keeper Remulos, its tranquil groves provide peace and deep communion with nature. For a young druid, learning to project one's spirit across the land into Moonglade via the teleportation spell is a critical step, granting constant access to the heart of druidic wisdom regardless of mortal distances.

While Moonglade is open to all who walk the path of the wild, it is not free of tension. A growing rift divides Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus and Keeper Remulos in Moonglade over the stewardship of nature and the creation of Teldrassil. Despite these philosophical fractures within the Cenarion Circle, young acolytes are still welcomed unconditionally into the haven of Nighthaven to pursue their sacred studies.

Arriving in Nighthaven brings the novice before Dendrite Starblaze, an elder tasked with guiding fledglings along the ways of the Claw. Before any initiate can claim the mantle of the bear, they must be immersed in its perspective: endurance, fury, and unyielding defense of the wild. Starblaze receives each new student with reverent deference to Father Cenarius, commencing the trials of the Great Bear Spirit.

The task reflects the fledgling Forsaken society's yearning to honor human ties and distinguish themselves from the mindless Scourge.

Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, Marla and Samuel Fipps lived together as husband and wife. When the plague swept through their lands, Samuel succumbed to the contagion and was reanimated as a mindless thrall of the Scourge. Though Marla was spared undeath, she could not escape Samuel himself, who brutally slew her in his mindless frenzy. Despite dying at her husband's hands, Marla harbored no hatred in her final moments. Her dying wish, remembered by Novice Elreth, was to rest eternally beside her husband in the Deathknell graveyard.

Novice Elreth dispatches Forsaken adventurers northeast of Deathknell to locate Samuel Fipps, who still wanders among a ruined campsite. Putting an end to Samuel's torment serves a dual purpose: it cleanses an encroaching Scourge minion from the valley and allows his physical remains to be carried back to Marla's resting place. As Elreth emphasizes, honoring the deceased and respecting their final wishes is a vital moral distinction separating the newly liberated Forsaken from the mindless malice of the Scourge.

Proving Grounds is an initiation rite given by Lieutenant Haggerdin to Alliance recruits enlisting with the Stormpike Guard in Alterac. Proving one's courage in the cavern marks the first step toward rising through the expedition's military ranks.

The Stormpike Guard wages a relentless campaign in Alterac Valley against the Frostwolf Clan. Lieutenant Haggerdin, coordinating forces from the Alliance encampment in the Alterac Mountains, refuses to send green recruits onto the battlefield without a test. Before granting any soldier an official place in the guard, Haggerdin demands proof of skill and nerve by sending them into the treacherous Icewing Caverns southwest of Dun Baldar.

The trial is straightforward in concept but deadly in execution: a Stormpike banner stands planted deep within the subterranean ice tunnels. The caverns are not empty; vicious frost harpies nest in the frostbitten recesses and eagerly tear apart unwary trespassers. Returning with the banner intact demonstrates that a recruit can navigate dangerous terrain, withstand brutal predators, and maintain discipline under pressure.

Surviving the cavern and returning the standard earns a soldier the Stormpike initiate's insignia, welcoming them officially into the expeditionary force. As Haggerdin promises, the insignia is not merely a trinket—it is a mark of rank that can be enhanced as a soldier earns greater honor on the battlefield, aspiring toward legendary honors such as the Eye of Command.
